# Dorrit Lornley

Dorrit Lornley is a Robotics Integration Engineer currently employed at Umbaly Cloud, a leading provider of autonomous rebar tying systems designed to improve speed and consistency on construction sites. Since joining Umbaly Cloud in 2020, Dorrit has focused on developing advanced autonomous controllers specifically tailored for rebar tying robots, a critical component in the broader domain of construction site robotics.

Career History

Dorrit began her career in 2014 as a robotics technician at BuildTech Innovations, where she contributed to early-stage prototypes of drone survey systems. In 2017, she transitioned to Titan Scaffold Corp., a major scaffold manufacturing and installation company, where she was promoted to lead engineer and spearheaded the company’s automation upgrade project. This initiative, internally codenamed Project IronClad, involved retrofitting existing scaffold assembly lines with robotic automation, cutting assembly time by 30% and reducing human errors significantly. Her work on Project IronClad earned her recognition among the company’s technical leadership for blending practical engineering solutions with scalable automation.

Specialties

Dorrit’s specialty lies in the design and tuning of autonomous control systems for mechanical arms used in rebar tying. She combines expertise in motion planning algorithms, sensor integration, and real-time feedback control to create systems that adapt dynamically to varying site conditions. Her proficiency with embedded systems and machine learning techniques also enables the robots to improve performance over time through data-driven adjustments.

Notable Projects at Umbaly Cloud

At Umbaly Cloud, Dorrit led the development of the Autotie Controller, a next-generation control platform that increased tying speed by 25% while maintaining a 99.8% tie accuracy rate. She also contributed to Project SkySurvey, integrating drone-based site scanning data to optimize robot paths in real time. Her collaboration with the safety monitoring team helped ensure robots operate safely alongside human workers.

Working Style and Collaborations

Known for a methodical and data-driven approach, Dorrit emphasizes iterative testing and cross-disciplinary teamwork. She frequently collaborates with software developers, mechanical engineers, and site safety officers to ensure the autonomous systems meet both operational and regulatory requirements. Her clear communication and hands-on leadership style foster a productive environment in the rapidly evolving field of construction robotics.
